segments.title: Chương 269: 0271
segments.content:
"Boss, Kai-Fu Lee from Google wants to meet with you."

"Ask him when he's free."

"He said he can come over to sit down anytime."

"Prepare some coffee for him, then."

ByteDance was in the Beida Science Park building, while Google China was in the Tsinghua Science Park building.

He really could come over for coffee anytime.

Chen Guiliang didn't have a good impression of Kai-Fu Lee, as the things he said and did were often quite outrageous.

The most disgusting instance was when Lin Miaoke was being harassed with vulgarities on Weibo, and she called for the deletion of harmful comments to clean up the Weibo environment.

Kai-Fu Lee, however, posted on Weibo telling Lin Miaoke: Harmful speech is a highly subjective judgment. Freedom of speech is an inalienable human right. The more you block speech, the more domineering and dictatorial you become. The angrier people get, the more you block them. Creating a healthy environment should involve tolerating more speech, not blocking people's right to speak.

He had actually branded a publicly insulted minor girl as a perpetrator who was depriving others of their freedom of speech.

Chen Guiliang didn't wait long before Kai-Fu Lee arrived.

And he had walked over.

The moment Kai-Fu Lee entered the company, many of ByteDance's employees turned their heads to look at him.

This was because Kai-Fu Lee was currently shrouded in too many halos of glory; he was admired and worshipped wherever he went.

Programmers, in particular, practically viewed Kai-Fu Lee as an idol.

Kai-Fu Lee was already used to this kind of treatment. He smiled and waved at the crowd, as if he were a high-level leader inspecting a local area.

Chen Guiliang walked out of his office to greet him, "Welcome, President Li. It's a pleasure to have you."

Kai-Fu Lee shook Chen Guiliang's hand and said, "Mr. Chen's websites are doing very well. They're the leader of China's SNS websites right now. I've come to learn from you, and to see if there's any chance for us to cooperate more deeply."

Chen Guiliang invited him into the meeting room.

Why did Kai-Fu Lee take the initiative to visit? It was, of course, because Chen Guiliang had fiercely attacked Baidu.

The enemy of my enemy is my friend.

While kicking Baidu when it was down, it was only natural for Google to seek cooperation with ByteDance.

Kai-Fu Lee maintained a smile the entire time. His demeanor was refined and composed, like a kind and gentle elder. Judging by his bearing and style, it was hard to guess that he was capable of doing so many despicable things.

After exchanging a few pleasantries in the meeting room, Kai-Fu Lee gradually got to the point: "Competition breeds progress. In any industry, it's not a good thing for one company to dominate. A monopoly only leads to the industry's decline."

Chen Guiliang nodded and said, "That is indeed true."

Kai-Fu Lee said, "Baidu's current market share is 56.6%. If it's allowed to continue developing, it will one day monopolize the search industry. That's why we at Google have come. And in just a few short months, we've brought our market share up to 32.8%."

Chen Guiliang asked bluntly, without holding back, "Is that 32.8% for Guge, or 32.8% for Google?"

Kai-Fu Lee said, "Guge is just the Chinese translation for Google."

Chen Guiliang smiled, not bothering to expose the lie directly.

Guge (domain suffix .cn) and Google (domain suffix .com) were, of course, different.

The former operated legally in China and was required to filter information.

The latter operated illegally in China and was not required to filter information.

And of the 32.8% market share Kai-Fu Lee mentioned, over 99% was contributed by the latter (illegal), while the former's (legal) contribution was less than 1%.

Furthermore, Guge (.cn)'s technical team currently consisted of only a handful of people. It was particularly difficult to use, with a user experience as awful as shit. It wouldn't see any significant improvements until the next year.

How would the average user know the difference between Guge and Google?

As the Golden Shield Project (the Great Firewall) was fully upgraded before the 2008 Olympics, Google.com became completely inaccessible in mainland China, leaving only Guge.cn, which had to filter harmful information. Consequently, its market share plummeted by 39% within a year!

This was the real reason Google withdrew from China—shrinking business and severe losses.

As for the claim that Google refused to comply with Chinese laws and regulations, that statement wasn't entirely accurate; it conflated the .cn and .com domains.

Guge (.cn) had engaged in illegal operations in areas like maps, but its information was filtered, yet its business never took off. Google (.com) had been operating illegally all along, and was finally blocked by the Great Firewall.

Chen Guiliang engaged in idle chatter, knowing what Kai-Fu Lee was getting at but not proactively taking the bait.

Kai-Fu Lee said, "I hope to establish a comprehensive partnership with ByteDance. For example, by embedding a Google search box in Xiaonei Wang and Hainei Wang, users can search the entire web from within the site. This would also be very convenient for Xiaonei Wang and Hainei Wang users."

Chen Guiliang said, "I need to confirm, are we embedding Google, or Guge? The former works very well, but is technically operating illegally. The latter is legal and compliant, but to be honest, it's far inferior to Baidu. The Chinese content it searches for is always completely irrelevant."

"The two are one and the same," Kai-Fu Lee continued to lie with a straight face.

This was Google's established operational strategy: to blur the distinction between Guge and Google. Never mind that ordinary netizens couldn't figure it out, even the government regulators were confused. The occasional official who knew would just turn a blind eye.

Chen Guiliang emphasized, "ByteDance is a law-abiding company. We do not cooperate with illegally operated websites."

The consistently refined and composed Kai-Fu Lee finally frowned.

He couldn't figure out if Chen Guiliang was pretending to be law-abiding, or if he was genuinely a good, law-abiding citizen.

The authorities hadn't even launched an investigation. Why was a company owner like him splitting hairs?

Google's development this year had been rather difficult; it was still in its initial stages.

If they could partner with Xiaonei Wang and Hainei Wang and embed the Google search box directly, it would be equivalent to a sudden surge of tens of millions of potential users.

Kai-Fu Lee took out a pack of American cigarettes and asked, "Do you smoke, Mr. Chen?"

Chen Guiliang took out his Zhonghua cigarettes. "Let's have these."

Kai-Fu Lee accepted a stick of Zhonghua, lit it, and exhaled clouds of smoke. "As long as ByteDance is willing to cooperate with Google, Google can open up some of its APIs. For example, Maps, Translate, Calendar, and so on."

Chen Guiliang lit his cigarette as well. He was slightly tempted.

But then he considered that Google would be pulling out of China in another four years. If he integrated these Google services, ByteDance's programmers would have to develop applications for them. By the time they perfected all the various applications, Google would just up and leave. Wouldn't that be a complete waste of effort?

However, these next few years were also a critical development period for ByteDance, and it seemed that partnering with Google could bring huge benefits.

After mulling it over for a while, Chen Guiliang asked again, "What else can Google offer me?"

Kai-Fu Lee said, "The internal search engines on Xiaonei Wang and Hainei Wang are not very well done, you could even say they're very poor. Google is willing to provide some search technology. ByteDance's programmers can regularly communicate with Google's programmers."

This was just him making empty promises.

Chen Guiliang found it amusing. "As far as I know, Guge.cn's search engine is not much better than ByteDance's internal search. The search technology team under you seems to only have a few people. Can you transfer programmers over from Google headquarters?"

Kai-Fu Lee said, "Although it's only a six-person team, I poached all of them from Microsoft Research Asia. I believe in their abilities. In the area of Chinese search, Google will see huge improvements by next year at the latest."

Chen Guiliang said, "I can also go to Microsoft Research Asia to poach people."

Kai-Fu Lee said, "You won't be able to. I was able to get them because of my connections and prestige from my time at Microsoft Research Asia."

Chen Guiliang remained noncommittal.

It was just a search engine, and not for the entire web, but just a vertical search within Xiaonei Wang and Hainei Wang.

There was an abundance of this kind of technical talent. ByteDance had already recruited several, and they were currently making steady improvements. A vertical search engine project like this could be done with a budget of two to three million.

If it were a full-web search engine, Chen Guiliang naturally wouldn't dare to attempt it, nor could he afford it. The R&D investment would easily be in the tens of millions, and even that would be considered a small-scale effort.

"I don't need this technology. What else can Google give me?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Having been rejected repeatedly, Kai-Fu Lee was already quite annoyed. "Young people shouldn't be so impatient. In a mutually beneficial partnership, you shouldn't make too many demands."

Chen Guiliang shook his head. "Because the terms of the partnership you've proposed are not equal. If Xiaonei Wang and Hainei Wang embed the Google search box, it's equivalent to giving Google our full support, which would be a huge help to Google's development. And what about Google? It's only opening up a few APIs like Maps and Translate. These kinds of commercial APIs are something Google will have to open up to more companies sooner or later as it develops its business. Wouldn't that be tantamount to ByteDance helping Google one-sidedly?"

Kai-Fu Lee said, "After embedding the Google search box, when users of Xiaonei Wang and Hainei Wang want to search the whole web, they won't have to leave the site to open Baidu."

Chen Guiliang said, "Google must show more sincerity for me to be willing to cooperate."

"Then let's both give it some more thought." Kai-Fu Lee stood up and shook his hand.

The situation at Google China was complex right now, and there were too many problems with a potential partnership.

Chen Guiliang went to discuss it with Guo Feng and was even more speechless after hearing his thoughts.

For example, if Google opened its APIs, it would definitely be the interfaces from its headquarters, because Google China didn't have those services yet. Google headquarters would certainly use the international standard REST API. But ByteDance, due to the Great Firewall, would tend to choose SOAP.

If the two sides disagreed, they would ultimately have to defer to Google's headquarters, and the resulting applications would be plagued with all sorts of delays and lags. The user experience would be absolutely terrible.

Kai-Fu Lee had been painting a pretty picture from the very beginning!

Chen Guiliang didn't understand much about technology and had almost been duped by the guy.

Guo Feng said, "Google China will definitely migrate all kinds of services over. Once their localization is well-established, it wouldn't be a bad idea to partner with them then. It's indeed too early to be talking about a partnership right now."

Chen Guiliang said, "You need to keep a closer eye on the internal search engines for Xiaonei Wang and Hainei Wang and do a good job. With the surge in users and content, what on earth is it searching for now? We're already getting a lot of negative feedback from users."

"You get what you pay for," Guo Feng said. "The six-person search engine team that Kai-Fu Lee poached from Microsoft Research Asia—any single one of them makes a much higher annual salary than I do."

Chen Guiliang instantly fell silent.

It really did come down to money.

Kai-Fu Lee left ByteDance and slowly strolled back to Tsinghua Science Park.

He was very displeased with Chen Guiliang, feeling that this young man was greedy and utterly disrespectful towards him, an elder in the industry.

Google had taken the initiative to seek a partnership, and he had even paid a personal visit. Any normal person would have happily agreed.

Yet Chen Guiliang had made demands again and again.

No wonder Li Yanhong got attacked so harshly.

(Recommending a new book by veteran entertainment genre author Bin Tie: "Chinese Entertainment 2000: Rising from a Beiying Boiler Worker".)
